title: Kyoto Police 'Overwhelmed' with Lost Items
paragraphs: Kyoto is one of the most popular cities in Japan for tourists. But the police in Kyoto are very busy with a different problem: lost items.

In Japan, when people find something that someone else has lost, they usually take it to the police. According to reports, the Kyoto Prefectural Police received about 630,000 found items in 2025. This was the second-highest number since the police started keeping records in 1971. The highest number was in 2024.
One police station in the center of the city, Nakagyo Police Station, received about 64,000 lost items in 2025 alone.

What kinds of things do people lose? The most common items are ID cards and other cards, such as driver's licenses and credit cards. These make up 48% of all cases. Wallets make up 10%, and mobile phones make up 7%. According to reports, the police also receive many wireless earbuds.

Tourists can make the work more difficult. Some tourists lose their things and then have to leave Japan very soon. This can make the process of returning lost items more complicated than usual. The police are also getting more reports from hotels.
The problem is not only in Kyoto. In Tokyo, for example, people handed in more than 4.5 million found items to the police in 2025.
Japan is famous for its honest people. Many visitors are surprised when their lost wallet or phone is returned to them. But all these lost items also mean a lot of extra work for the police.
